The function assumes the API object exposes an action method it may not actually have, instead of checking the available interface and handling the result in a supported way. General rule: don’t hard-code assumptions about external APIs’ methods or capabilities; validate the contract and keep computation separate from execution.

The function is too rigid: it assumes every client’s terms reduce to simple “invoice date + net days” and an optional early-payment discount, so it can miscompute both amount and due date when the real terms have different structure or settlement rules. General rule: always interpret the full terms schema instead of hard-coding one payment model.

The function is too heuristic about payment timing: it scans nested terms for anything date-like and may pick the wrong rule or the earliest-looking date instead of the vendor’s actual due-date term.  

General rule: for scheduling inputs, always resolve the payment date from the single authoritative term field/schema, not by guessing from multiple candidate dates.

The function is too eager to “guess” from partial matches in a nested terms object: it may pick the wrong rule or the wrong field and then treat that as the full payment instruction.  
General rule: don’t infer payment amount/date from the first vaguely matching term; first identify the actual governing term block and then compute strictly from its explicit terms.

The function is too eager to interpret any payment-like field as the actual terms, so it can pick the wrong rule or wrong date basis when the client’s terms are structured or ambiguous. The general rule is: **don’t guess from loosely matching fields; resolve the authoritative terms schema and apply its precedence exactly.**

The function over-trusts loose text patterns: it grabs the wrong numbers from mixed-content lines and assumes every relevant field will appear under an exact label like “subtotal” or “freight.” General rule: **don’t do naive string matching on semi-structured documents; parse only explicit field labels and validate extracted values against the document’s summary/totals.**

The function is too label-dependent: it only extracts values when they appear next to the exact field names it knows, so it misses invoices that state key details in different wording or in the body text. General rule: for semi-structured documents, don’t rely only on explicit labels—also derive totals and charges from itemized lines and recognize common synonyms/variants in phrasing.
